newsitem.title: USA: US High Court denies appeal in BankBoston case.
newsitem.headline: US High Court denies appeal in BankBoston case.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday denied an appeal by three individuals over the legal fees in a class-action lawsuit settlement involving BankBoston Corp and its affiliates involving mortgage servicing.

The three individuals sued in federal court against their initial lawyers, the bank and the bank's lawyers, charging fraud, malpractice and other offenses. They sued because the attorney fees they had to pay far exceeded the amount awarded.
The class-action lawsuit had been filed in state court in Alabama contending that the bank and its affiliates did not promptly post interest to real estate escrow accounts.
A settlement was reached and approved by a state judge in 1994.

Under the settlement, the bank disbursed more than $8 million to the attorneys who brought the suit and credited each of the estimated 715,000 members of the nationwide class-action suit with small amounts, totaling less than $9.
Dexter Kamilewicz, one of the three individuals who brought the suit, received $2.19, but had to pay $91.33 in legal fees.

A federal judge and a U.S. Court of Appeals in Chicago dismissed the suit, saying federal courts lacked jurisdiction. The judge said he was barred from considering an attack on the state court judgment and issues interwined with it.

Twenty-two states supported the appeal by the three individuals asking the Supreme Court to hear the case and rule that the federal lawsuit can go forward. But the justices denied the appeal without any comment or dissent.
